newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says hopes Ross deals with settlements.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says hopes Ross deals with settlements.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said on Sunday he hoped U.S. envoy Dennis Ross would find a way to deal with Jewish settlements during his current visit to the Middle East.

"Dennis Ross is currently in the region in an attempt to overcome obstacles that stand in the way of the Palestinian-Israeli track of the peace process and the first and most important of these obstacles is the settlements issue in Jabal Abu Ghneim," Moussa told reporters.
"I hope Ross's visit will lead to ways of dealing with the problem of settlements and the Jabal Abu Ghneim problem -- this would be the measure of success of his mission," he added.
Moussa was referring to the new Jewish settlement of Har Homa that Israel began in March in Arab East Jerusalem, occupied in 1967 by Israel.

Talks between the Palestinians and Israel have been halted since the ground breaking and a subsequent attack on a Tel Aviv cafe that killed an Arab bomber and three Israelis. Palestinians refuse to resume talks until settlement activities are halted.
Ross, on his second mission to the region in a month, met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in the Sinai resort of Sharm el-Sheikh on Saturday about the stalled talks.
The U.S. envoy is expected to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the West Bank city of Ramallah later on Sunday.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu forecast on Sunday it would "take some time" before Ross would be able to get Israel and the PLO to talk peace again.
Moussa said: "Reviving the peace process depends mainly on halting the policy of settlements."
The Egyptian minister discussed the crisis in the peace process with Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani earlier on Sunday.
